notes: A realistic first-person tactical shooter with breaching, leaning, prone and objective play is the Tactical Shooter preset and the genre's MilSim case exactly, so the map is a raid site of rooms that dead-end into breach points rather than an arcade lane network; the author's choice of an industrial complex for the first map was made on the strength of close-quarters breaches and vertical routes, which confirms rooms-sequence. Interiors are the whole game here — players breach doors, clear rooms and climb through windows — so P3 is required rather than assumed, and I built the vertical routes as stair- and ladder-reached mezzanines and rooftops, which is tiered, rather than catwalks overhanging the floor, keeping this off the P2 pipeline that is not ready. I added choke-bottleneck for the breach points, which MilSim wants deliberately exposed, and capture-zone for the hostage, explosive and intelligence objectives. With no user to ask, I scoped the build to the single industrial complex the author named and deferred the other map settings, so no P4; I read the destructible walls and barricades as a request no Shooter option covers, since the genre has no destructible row, and treated vehicles, weather, day-night, damage and attachment systems as non-layout. The two squad spawns are one staging position per side per the MilSim note, not mirrored respawning bases.
